ubiquitous.definition: Present, appearing, or found everywhere at the same time.
ubiquitous.example: Smartphones have become ubiquitous in modern urban life.

ephemeral.definition: Lasting for a very short time; transitory; fleeting.
ephemeral.example: Fame in the internet age can be remarkably ephemeral.

serendipity.definition: The occurrence and development of events by chance in a happy or beneficial way.
serendipity.example: Discovering penicillin was a triumph of scientific serendipity.

pragmatic.definition: Dealing with things sensibly and realistically in a way that is based on practical rather than theoretical considerations.
pragmatic.example: She took a pragmatic approach to solving the team's resource constraints.

meticulous.definition: Showing great attention to detail; very careful and precise.
meticulous.example: The software engineer did a meticulous review of the security logs.

expedite.definition: To make an action or process happen sooner or be accomplished more quickly.
expedite.example: We automated our deployment pipeline to expedite feature delivery.

resilient.definition: Able to withstand or recover quickly from difficult conditions or shocks.
resilient.example: Distributed state machines are designed to be resilient under node failure.

lucid.definition: Expressed clearly; easy to understand; showing the ability to think clearly.
lucid.example: His architecture explanation was so lucid that even junior developers grasped it.

eloquent.definition: Fluent or persuasive in speaking or writing; clearly expressing or indicating something.
eloquent.example: She delivered an eloquent defense of user privacy principles.

superfluous.definition: Unnecessary, especially through being more than enough.
superfluous.example: The refactoring eliminated superfluous database queries.

mercurial.definition: Subject to sudden or unpredictable changes of mood or mind.
mercurial.example: Her mercurial temperament made design critiques intensely exciting.

tenacious.definition: Tending to keep a firm hold of something; clinging or adhering closely; persistent.
tenacious.example: He had a tenacious grip on the technical requirements.
